title: Leading With Nexus
description: For managers and above: how to run a team on Nexus. The leader's day, approvals, shifts and the planner, Time Sheet review, the scorecard, the ticket desk, people from hiring to exits, training the team, communicating, the money and property views, and access, settings and the record.
overview: The leader's day: decisions, the team's view, the Team widgets
Approvals: the recommendation, punch fixes, phones and delegates
Shifts and the planner: rules that warn, Save & Share, Confirm and the day's notices
Time Sheet review in People > Time: approve or send back; only the employee signs
The ticket desk: queues, the Next Clock, Preventive, what stays private
People: hiring, onboarding, probation, performance, exits
Training your team and keeping courses current
Communicating: announcements, Teams, Notes and Boards
Money and property views; access, settings and the record
teaches: Dashboard, Approvals, Team, Shifts, Time Sheet, Time Off, Workforce Analytics, Tickets, People, Hiring, Checklists, Performance, Training, Announcements, Notes, Boards, Settings, Asset Management, Accounting

questions.q: You are a new manager and your Dashboard still shows only your own Home widgets. Where do you find the team ones?
options: Workday, then the My Team tab at the top
questions.explanation: Click Customize, then Add Widget; the Team category holds the leader's widgets, such as Team Clocked-In and Time Exceptions.

questions.q: Marco asks for a 5:00 PM clock-out and his End of Day message posted at 5:02 PM. What do you do?
options: Send it back for a ticket number
Reject it and tell him on Teams
questions.explanation: The record supports the time he asks for, so it is a quick yes. Evidence decides a punch fix.

questions.q: A time off request reads Check First. What does that mean?
options: Look at the reasons, then decide
Nexus has already rejected the request
HR must approve it before you can
questions.explanation: Check First flags something to look at, with reasons. It is advice, not a no; nothing in Nexus approves or rejects by itself.

questions.q: You leave for a week of approved vacation tomorrow. What do you set today?
questions.explanation: Delegate My Approvals, at the bottom of Workday > Time Off, hands your approvals to a colleague for the days you are away.

questions.q: Sharing a week that breaks the six-days-in-a-row rule is blocked until you fix it.
questions.explanation: False. The rules warn and never block. Sharing past a warning asks for a reason that only managers see.

questions.q: Two people on your team have not confirmed next week's shared schedule. What is the fastest step?
options: Share the whole week again from the planner
Text each of them the schedule
Ask HR to send a reminder
questions.explanation: The confirmed chip lists who has not confirmed, with Nudge and Nudge Everyone.

questions.q: A flagged Time Sheet has an open punch fix request. What do you decide first?
questions.explanation: An approved request changes the hours, and approval waits until no change request is pending.

questions.q: After you approve a Time Sheet, the employee is the only one who signs it.
questions.explanation: True. Your approval is a review recorded on the PDF; only the employee signs.

lessons.checkpoint: Checkpoint: The Desk, People and Training

questions.q: Sam scores 32 of 40 hours, with Thursday empty against a shared shift. What do you check first?
options: His pay for the week, in People > Time first
His Workforce Scorecard grant level and scope
That day's No-Show bell and his messages
questions.explanation: A gap is a fact to read with the schedule. He may have forgotten to punch, worked elsewhere, or not shown.

questions.q: A part-time teammate shows No Schedule on the scorecard. Why?
options: No shifts were shared for them
They missed every shift that was shared that week
The scorecard has not loaded their punches yet
questions.explanation: Part-time staff with no shared shifts are never guessed. Share their shifts if you want them scored.

questions.q: You open the ticket desk at 8:30 AM. Which queue do you work first?
questions.explanation: Needs Reply is where a requester is waiting on the desk. Work it first, every hour you are at the desk.

questions.q: A ticket has sat in Unassigned since last night. Who do you assign it to?
questions.explanation: Assign to a person the day it arrives. A ticket with a name has a clock someone feels.

questions.q: A leader with the Tickets grant can see Ask HR tickets from their own team.
questions.explanation: False. Confidential HR tickets are visible only to HR's audience, never to the person's manager.

questions.q: Priya asks you why her paycheck looked short. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Pay and the record are HR's, and Ask HR keeps the question private from the manager by design.

questions.q: Priya's probation is ending and she has done well. What do you click?
questions.explanation: Confirm is your recommendation; HR finalizes, and the letter goes to Priya alone to sign.

questions.q: Marco is locked out of a quiz after three tries. What comes before Unlock?
options: A ticket to the course owner
A talk about what to reread
A new course assignment for next month
questions.explanation: Look at his misses on the course's report and talk it through first; then unlock another round.

questions.q: Gate hours change next month at every California site. Who posts the announcement?
questions.explanation: Administrators post announcements. A leader asks, often with the wording drafted.

lessons.title: Words to Know
lessons.summary: The Academy's glossary: every leader's word from this course, with what it means, in one place.

questions.q: Which two things does a leader check every morning?
options: Pay figures and the labor budget for the site
The Catalog and each person's Refresher
Who is here and what waits on you
questions.explanation: Who is here (clocked in, late, out) and what is waiting on you (approvals and the bell).

questions.q: You approve a teammate's day off in the hallway. When is it approved?
options: As soon as you say yes
questions.explanation: A decision made anywhere else leaves no record and tells nobody. It is approved when it is decided in Nexus.

questions.q: Managers can add more Team widgets than Supervisors.
questions.explanation: True. Supervisors get Team Clocked-In, Who Has What, My Ticket Queue and My Team; Managers also get the approval and time widgets.

questions.q: Which Team widget shows who on your team is on the clock right now?
questions.explanation: Team Clocked-In shows who is in. Time Exceptions shows who is late or has a break still open.

questions.q: Sam asks for a 6:30 PM clock-out with no message and no ticket after his 5:30 PM shift end. What do you do?
options: Approve it now to save everyone time
Change the punch to 5:30 PM yourself
Send it back asking what kept him
questions.explanation: The record does not support it yet. Send it back saying what you need; never edit a punch yourself.

questions.q: You approved the wrong request a second ago in Approvals. What catches it?
questions.explanation: A decision leaves the list at once and is sent after a few seconds, so Undo catches a slip.

questions.q: Approvals on a phone has no bulk approve.
questions.explanation: True. On a phone it is one card at a time with two decisions, so each decision is read before it is made.

questions.q: You reject a time off request. What else must you do?
options: Delete the request so it leaves the list
Tell HR about it the same day
questions.explanation: A no with a reason lets the person ask for different days and makes the decision stand.

questions.q: Who can you pick as a delegate for your approvals?
options: Anyone on your own team who is working
Any employee at the same site
A peer or your own manager
questions.explanation: A delegate is your manager, a peer, or someone at your level or above, never your own team.

questions.q: How quickly should a time off request be answered?
questions.explanation: A request that waits a week is a plan the person cannot make.

questions.q: You want each person's usual hours laid across next week. Which tool?
questions.explanation: Fill Automatically lays usual hours across a date range; Copy Week repeats a past week. Both skip holidays and approved time off.

questions.q: Copy Week skipped Marco's Saturday. Why?
options: The six-days rule blocked that day
He has not confirmed his schedule yet
questions.explanation: Fill Automatically and Copy Week skip each person's holidays and approved time off, and say how many days they skipped.

questions.q: A shift you placed with a dashed border can already be seen by the team.
questions.explanation: False. A dashed border is a draft. Nothing reaches the team until you Save & Share.

questions.q: You share a week over a rest-time warning and type a reason. Who can read it?
options: The whole team, on Team > Shifts
Nobody; the reason is never stored anywhere
questions.explanation: The reason is for the record, kept in the shift's History, and staff never see it.

questions.q: A teammate punches in 40 minutes early without being asked. What does Nexus do?
options: Records it and sends one grouped bell
Blocks the punch until the shift starts
questions.explanation: An early punch is never blocked. You get one grouped bell per team and day; a habit is a conversation.

questions.q: Where do you look for the labor cost of next week's schedule?
options: Team > Shifts, under each person's hours
Nowhere; managers do not see it
The Shift Planner footer, beside the hours
questions.explanation: The planner shows hours, never wages. Labor cost and the labor budget are for HR and above.

questions.q: Shift swaps are off unless your company turns them on.
questions.explanation: True. Trading, releases and open-shift requests are off by default, switched on per company in Settings > Shifts & Scheduling.

questions.q: Where do Time Sheets wait for your review after the period ends?
questions.explanation: People > Time lists Time Sheets to Review. Your own Workday tab shows only Time Sheets waiting on your signature.

questions.q: Seven Time Sheets have no flags. What handles them fastest?
questions.explanation: Review All Clean walks through the unflagged ones; Approve Reviewed approves only those you ticked.

questions.q: Thursday is missing a shift on a Time Sheet. What do you do?
questions.explanation: A send-back says exactly what to fix, and the card comes back to you when it is fixed.

questions.q: A California-rule hourly worker reports a missed meal break. What do you add?
options: A note on the person's Board
A written warning to the person
questions.explanation: You add the premium pay the company's rule sets, and the corrected card goes back for signature.

questions.q: Changing hours on a Time Sheet you already approved sends it back to you to approve again.
questions.explanation: True. A punch fix, your own edit or a decline in Nexus Sign reopens the period.

questions.q: A teammate who left never signed an approved Time Sheet. Who finalizes it?
questions.explanation: HR finalizes an unsigned card with a reason; never a manager, and never by skipping the signature.

questions.q: When should you review Time Sheets?
options: Whenever HR sends you a reminder
The day after the period ends
At the end of the following month
questions.explanation: Payroll runs from signed, final Time Sheets, and every day of waiting delays it.

questions.q: Which grant level shows a manager only their direct reports on the Scorecard?
questions.explanation: Viewer is direct reports, Editor the whole reporting line, Full the company.

questions.q: A teammate had approved time off Wednesday. How does the scorecard treat that day?
questions.explanation: Holidays and approved time off excuse the day, and a Sick or PTO punch covers it.

questions.q: A red week on the scorecard means the person's pay will be docked.
questions.explanation: False. The scorecard measures attendance against expectation; the Time Sheet is the pay record.

questions.q: Where is the Workforce Scorecard?
questions.explanation: It is a tab inside Team > Workforce Analytics, and it opens only with the Workforce Scorecard grant.

questions.q: A teammate asks how the analytics are used. Where is the answer?
options: Your own judgment as their manager
questions.explanation: Each company's Workforce Analytics policy, set in Settings > Workforce Analytics, says what is measured and how it is used.

questions.q: A row's Next Clock turns red. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: The Next Clock is the one deadline wording on the list and turns red only when overdue.

questions.q: A ticket is waiting on a gate vendor. What must it carry?
options: The vendor and the promised date
A photo of the vendor's truck at the gate
The invoice total from the vendor's quote
questions.explanation: Waiting for Vendor is a status, not a parking space; the desk still owes the requester updates.

questions.q: The Preventive queue shows 2 in red. What does that count?
options: Vendors still waiting on a work order
All open tickets on the whole desk
questions.explanation: The Preventive count is the overdue ones. Zero overdue means the building is being kept.

questions.q: Resolving a preventive ticket needs a photo.
questions.explanation: True. Closing it writes the maintenance record and moves the schedule on.

questions.q: Where are Due Soon and Waiting on the desk?
questions.explanation: Needs Reply, Unassigned, Mine and All Open stand as tabs; the rest sit under Other Queues.

questions.q: Which part of a direct report's record can a manager change?
options: Their bank details for direct deposit
Their job title, if HR agrees
questions.explanation: Name, title, department, pay and bank details are HR's. A manager changes the team's day: shifts, checklist steps, goals.

questions.q: An offer letter is signed by the company first, then the candidate.
questions.explanation: False. The company never signs before the employee; an offer letter is signed by the candidate only.

questions.q: A checklist step for a new hire is yours. Where does it reach you?
options: As an email from HR with a link
As a task on My Tasks
questions.explanation: Each checklist step reaches its owner as a subtask on My Tasks; tick it there and the checklist moves.

questions.q: Where do you find your team's goals and 1:1s?
questions.explanation: A manager's view of their people's performance pages is under Workday > Performance > My Team.

questions.q: A teammate is leaving. How does the exit start?
options: You delete their future shifts in the planner
questions.explanation: An exit runs one way. Nexus then clears shifts, ends access on the date and brings equipment due.

questions.q: An escalation says Sam is six days overdue on a course. What is the best first step?
options: Reassign the course to next quarter
Ask what is in the way
Note it on his record for review
questions.explanation: An escalation is a nudge to a conversation. Often the fix is time on the schedule.

questions.q: Where do you see your direct reports' training status?
questions.explanation: Manage > Compliance shows your people; Training > Compliance is your own record.

questions.q: Which part of a course's report shows the questions people miss most?
questions.explanation: A hard question is a lesson that did not land or a question that is wrong. Tell the course owner.

questions.q: You may use Sign Off a Person for work a trainer told you about but you did not see.
questions.explanation: False. An in-person sign-off is only for work the person signing it saw.

questions.q: A teammate passed a course months ago and gets three questions a day from it. What is that?
questions.explanation: The Refresher asks three questions a day on a widening schedule. It is never a score and never yours to chase.

questions.q: A screen that a course teaches changes. What does Nexus do with the course?
options: Deletes the course and its certificates
questions.explanation: A course flagged for review is read against the new screen; the owner publishes edits or clicks Mark Reviewed.

questions.q: Your announcement needs proof each person read it. Which option do you ask for?
questions.explanation: Acknowledge records who has read it, and the poster sees the short list of who has not.

questions.q: Where do you message a teammate from Nexus?
options: A Nexus chat window in the sidebar
A shared Note that mentions them by name
questions.explanation: Nexus has no chat of its own. The Teams buttons beside every person open Teams to them.

questions.q: Typing a teammate's name in a note notifies them.
questions.explanation: False. A mention in a note notifies nobody. A problem that someone must act on goes in a ticket or a form.

questions.q: You need a marked-up photo of canopy damage on its ticket. What do you use?
questions.explanation: Mark Up opens a Board with the picture placed, and the marked-up image can be attached back to the ticket.

questions.q: Repairs are up on your site's Income Statement. How do you see what is behind the figure?
options: Ask HR for a payroll report for the site
questions.explanation: Every figure drills down to its ledger lines and on to the transaction behind it.

questions.q: Which Asset Management card shows what the property's record is missing?
questions.explanation: Data Gaps shows what the record lacks; Needs Attention shows what is due or warning.

questions.q: A purchase request asks for a pressure washer. What do you check first?
options: The vendor's reviews and its delivery dates
questions.explanation: Item Management may already have one. Then the justification and your limit.

questions.q: A site leader sees the team's wages in Accounting.
questions.explanation: False. Pay stays with HR; a site leader reads the entity's statements, not payroll.

questions.q: Which tier can see across company walls?
options: Any tier with an Access Group grant
questions.explanation: An Administrator is always walled. Only a Super Administrator, or a member of a group flagged as global, crosses.

questions.q: A new teammate cannot see the ticket desk. What is usually missing?
questions.explanation: Most "I can't see it" questions are a missing grant. Ask your administrator to add them to the right Access Group.

questions.q: What does the screen show under a person's name?
options: Their company wall and access level
questions.explanation: The job title shows as words; the tier is only a small mark beside the name.

questions.q: A teammate wants to start before their access is set up. What do you do?
options: Share your sign-in for a day
questions.explanation: A shared sign-in makes every punch, approval and signature under it someone else's.

questions.q: Administrators see and work tickets from every company.
questions.explanation: True. Tickets are the one exception to the walls; the people pickers still stay inside each company.

questions.q: Which of these is on the leader's every-week list?
options: Read the scorecard with the schedule
Review every Time Sheet the team signed
questions.explanation: Each week: share the schedule, read the scorecard with the schedule beside it, and check Compliance.
